report:
The scoped analytic counterexample is sound. This verdict does not certify a resolution of P19.1: the submission establishes failure of an unrestricted entropy-slope equality determined solely by the ordinary non-Archimedean datum, and explicitly leaves the residual maximal-ray question unresolved. P19.2–P19.4 are unclaimed.

The Cantor construction works. Every level-j interval has mass 2^{-j} and diameter exp(-4^j), giving ψ(x)≤−2^j on K. The logarithmic potential itself is upper semicontinuous by reverse Fatou, so taking its psh representative does not erase these poles. Uniform local integrability of the logarithmic kernel establishes ψ∈L¹. Outside K its curvature is ω; consequently the non-pluripolar mass of τψ is 1−τ. The exponential-integrability proof is also valid: atomlessness permits a neighborhood of mass q with bq<2, and Jensen followed by Fubini reduces the estimate to the integrable planar kernel |z−w|^{-bq}. Each fixed b receives its own finite constant.

The envelope theorem applies because τψ≤0 and 1−τ>0 throughout 0<τ<a<1. The submitted concavity argument, almost-everywhere identification of decreasing parameter limits, and endpoint sandwich establish every test-curve condition, including P[χ_a]=χ_a. No endpoint mass-continuity assertion is needed in the energy integral. The bounded maximal-test-curve correspondence therefore produces an actual weak geodesic ray from zero. Its mass profile gives E(r_t)=(a−a²/2)t and E(v_t)=−a²t/2. The bounds −at≤v_t≤0 and v_t≥aψ follow directly from the Legendre transform.

The entropy estimate has the correct sign. Bounded-potential integration by parts gives ∫(−v)MA(v)≥−E(v). Applying the proved entropy inequality to the bounded function −bv_t, and using v_t≥aψ, yields Ent(v_t)≥ba²t/2−log C_ab. Taking t→∞ separately for each b, then allowing b to increase, proves the extended-real limit +∞. Neither finite entropy at every time nor uniform control of C_ab as b→∞ is needed or claimed.

The total-space argument establishes the actual datum. Local smooth potentials reduce removability across the central fiber to the psh extension theorem. Every exponential power remains locally integrable there. On a modification, a positive generic divisorial coefficient λ implies U∘π≤λ log|z₁|+C by subtraction of the divisorial current. With Jacobian vanishing order k, change of variables would require integrability of |z₁|^{-bλ+2k}, which fails when bλ≥2(k+1). Thus every divisorial coefficient vanishes, including those above the central fiber. Divisorial determination identifies the datum with zero; this is stronger than merely checking finite-time slices. The trivial configuration has one central component of multiplicity one and intersection weight V_X/V_X=1. With discrepancy over X normalized at the trivial valuation, its non-Archimedean entropy is zero.

The product argument also checks out. Restricting a Perron competitor to a curve fiber gives a curve competitor or an identically −∞ function; either lies below the curve geodesic. The pullback supplies the reverse envelope inequality. Bedford–Taylor calculus gives Θ_u^{m+1}=(m+1)ω_v⊗η^m, so probability normalization cancels the binomial coefficient. Directly in the energy sum, Θ_u^j∧Θ^{m+1−j}=[jω_v+(m+1−j)ω]⊗η^m; summing proves E_Θ(p₁*v)=E_ω(v), including m=0. The common second probability factor preserves entropy exactly. Fubini extends exponential integrability, and the same transverse-coordinate argument proves zero total-space divisorial coefficients in every product dimension.

The nonprojective and transcendental assertions have their stated scope. A projective embedding of X would restrict to a projective embedding of Y. Nonprojective two-dimensional tori exist: generic complex structures on R⁴/Z⁴ avoid the countably many proper loci where a nonzero integral alternating form becomes J-invariant; translation-invariant Hermitian metrics are Kähler, while the Riemann criterion excludes projectivity. Restricting the product class to Y also preserves its asserted transcendental character.

Two harmless clarifications are appropriate. Darvas–Xia use ddᶜ=i/(2π)∂∂̄, whereas the submission uses i/π; applying their analytic correspondence with background ω/2 rescales currents and volumes together and leaves the normalized energy formula unchanged. Also, “only three established inputs” should mean three principal specialized inputs: the standard product calculus, integration by parts, removability, and divisorial-current subtraction are additional background results, enumerated below. Neither clarification requires a new construction.

The constructed ray is not maximal relative to its datum: the zero ray has the same initial potential and datum and dominates it, with strict inequality forced by its negative energy. Accordingly, it does not contradict the catalogue’s maximal-ray scope. The task allows explicitly scoped partial progress, but does not identify the unrestricted equality rejected here as the complete residual statement. No active atomic target is established as solved by this submission.
premises: Let M be a compact Kähler manifold and θ a smooth closed real (1,1)-form representing a big class. For f∈PSH(M,θ) with f≤0 and positive non-pluripolar top mass, define Pθ[f]=(lim_{C→∞}Pθ(f+C,0))* using rooftop envelopes. Then f≤Pθ[f]≤0, Pθ[f] has the same non-pluripolar top mass as f, and Pθ[Pθ[f]]=Pθ[f]. [Darvas–Di Nezza–Lu, §3.2 and Theorem 3.12](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1705.05796v3).

Let (M,θ) be compact Kähler, V=∫Mθⁿ, and χτ a test curve of θ-psh potentials or −∞: for every x its parameter dependence is concave, decreasing and upper semicontinuous; χτ≡0 for sufficiently negative τ, χτ≡−∞ for sufficiently positive τ, and Pθ[χτ]=χτ. Set A=inf{τ:χτ≡−∞}. Then r_t=supτ(χτ+tτ) is a weak geodesic ray from zero, bounded at every finite time, and its normalized Aubin–Mabuchi energy satisfies Eθ(r_t)=t[A+∫_{−∞}^A(V⁻¹∫M⟨θ_{χτ}ⁿ⟩−1)dτ]. [Darvas–Xia, Theorem 3.7(iii)–(iv), Proposition 3.8 and Definition 3.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2003.04818).

For a compact Kähler manifold (M,θ), a nonpositive psh ray has a divisorial non-Archimedean datum obtained from the negative divisorial singularity numbers of its S¹-invariant total potential on normalized Gauss extensions. This datum extends uniquely to a [θ]-psh function on Mℶ. More generally, [θ]-psh functions are determined by their values on divisorial valuations. [Mesquita–Piccione, §5.1, Theorem 5.1.4, Remark 5.1.5 and Theorem 4.3.8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.06221v2).

Locally bounded psh potentials on a complex manifold have well-defined positive Bedford–Taylor products, symmetric and multilinear in their associated closed (1,1)-currents, with continuity under locally uniformly bounded decreasing psh sequences. For one psh potential f, its non-pluripolar current is ⟨ddᶜf⟩=1_{f>−∞}ddᶜf. [Boucksom–Eyssidieux–Guedj–Zeriahi, §1.2 and Proposition 1.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674).

Every bounded quasi-psh function f on a compact Riemann surface has finite Dirichlet energy and satisfies ∫f ddᶜf=−∫df∧dᶜf≤0, with the bounded-potential interpretation of the integrals. [Boucksom–Eyssidieux–Guedj–Zeriahi, Theorem 1.14](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674).

Let A be a closed pluripolar subset of a complex manifold M. Every psh function on M\A that is locally bounded above near A extends uniquely to a psh function on M, given by upper semicontinuous extension. [Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter I, Theorem 5.24](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf).

Let T be a closed positive (1,1)-current on a complex manifold and F an irreducible analytic hypersurface. If λ is the generic Lelong number of T along F, then T−λ[F] is a closed positive current. [Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter III, §8, divisorial-current subtraction and Siu decomposition](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf).

Let M be compact Kähler of dimension n, α a Kähler class with Vα=αⁿ>0, and φ_D∈H(α) represented by a vertical divisor D on a smooth snc test configuration 𝓜 dominating M×P¹. Writing 𝓜₀=Σ_F b_FF, its normalized model Monge–Ampère measure is Σ_F b_F[((α_𝓜+D)|_F)ⁿ/Vα]δ_{v_F}, where v_F is the normalized associated valuation. [Mesquita–Piccione, §4.2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.06221v2).

For a compact Kähler manifold (M,θ), α=[θ], φ∈E¹(α) and u₀∈E¹(θ), there exists a unique maximal finite-energy geodesic ray starting at u₀ with non-Archimedean datum φ. Maximality means dominance over geodesic rays with smaller initial potential and smaller non-Archimedean datum. [Mesquita–Piccione, Definition 5.1.6 and Theorem 5.1.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.06221v2).

A compact complex torus Cᵈ/Λ, with Λ a full lattice, is projective if and only if there exists a positive definite Hermitian form h on Cᵈ such that Im h(λ₁,λ₂)∈Z for every λ₁,λ₂∈Λ. [Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter VII, Corollary 14.5](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf).
